covers: The Z80's fixed vectors: reset, the eight restarts and the non-maskable interrupt. Interrupt mode 2 reads its handler from a table at the I register and the data byte, so it has no fixed address; mode 0 executes an opcode from the bus, covered by the restarts; the NSC800's own interrupt addresses belong to another cpu type

entries.name: reset, RST 00h
entries.description: Where execution starts after a reset, and the target of the RST 00h instruction.
entries.behaviour: A reset clears the program counter, so execution begins at this address. The one-byte RST 00h instruction (opcode C7) calls it after pushing the return address.

entries.description: Target of the RST 38h instruction and of a maskable interrupt in interrupt mode 1.
entries.behaviour: The one-byte RST 38h instruction (opcode FF) calls this address after pushing the return address. In interrupt mode 1 a maskable interrupt clears both interrupt flip-flops, pushes the program counter and jumps here.

entries.name: NMI
entries.behaviour: A falling edge on the NMI pin is always accepted at the end of the current instruction, whatever the interrupt enable flip-flop holds. The CPU clears the first flip-flop, leaves the second holding its old state, pushes the program counter and jumps here. RETN copies the second flip-flop back into the first.
